text: Because it is soaked in the continuum, the first-order theory of elementary Euclidean geometry is incomplete and undecidable, exactly as Gödel's theorems make arithmetic.
explanation: False. Tarski proved the opposite: elementary Euclidean geometry is consistent, complete, and decidable, because it is bi-interpretable with real-closed fields, which admit quantifier elimination. Richness in the continuum does not cause incompleteness — only the ability to interpret arithmetic does.
